Falsy and absent are different.

Defaults apply to absence, not failed conversion. Handle those failures explicitly and add application range checks where required; no patch is needed.

DC-C02: RepositoryEnv is a file snapshot created in __init__; the old instance retains first after the file edit, while a new one reads second. Config checks environment on each get, so environment-one then environment-two can override that same repository dynamically. DC-U02: Default UTF-8 retains a leading U+FEFF as part of the first key, so the expected unprefixed key is absent. Existing RepositoryEnv(path, encoding='utf-8-sig') handles the initial BOM and preserves the Chinese value and embedded a<U+FEFF>b character. A library patch or global removal of U+FEFF is unnecessary and could corrupt data.
DC-C03: RepositoryEnv uses a simple first-equals split with outer-quote removal. export VB_CASE_EXPORT is literally the key; # inside a value and later equals remain data, and the matching outer quotes around coffee beans are removed. It is not a shell or a universal dotenv parser and does not execute or interpolate shell syntax. Supply compatible simple inputs or use an explicitly selected parser boundary.
DC-U03: The helper uses shlex: # begins a comment, a backslash escapes the following character, and consecutive delimiter whitespace drops empty fields. Thus coffee#roast,tea yields coffee, the backslash before d is removed, and coffee,,tea has two items. Quoted coffee, beans stays one item. Item cast runs before post_process, so Csv(cast=int, post_process=tuple) gives (1, 2). This is not lossless standard CSV parsing.
DC-C04: Keep the legacy Csv default for existing callers and use the existing arbitrary callable cast for this value, for example lambda value: next(csv.reader([value], strict=True)). Standard CSV preserves coffee#roast, the empty middle field and the literal backslash-d-plus field; strict quote handling makes malformed input a deliberate conversion failure. No library modification is required for this one-record application policy.
